free_tier.stated: USD 14/year for Xeon-1 in Atlanta: 1 vCPU, 1 GB RAM, 10 GB SSD, 2.5 TB of monthly bandwidth counting both directions, a 500 Mbps port and 1 IPv4. Xeon-2 is USD 24/year for 2 GB, 20 GB and 5 TB; Xeon-4 is USD 34/year for 2 vCPU, 4 GB, 40 GB and 10 TB; the EPYC line offers EPYC-8 at USD 10/month for 4 vCPU, 8 GB, 100 GB, 15 TB and a 5 Gbps port. All promotional prices are stated to be recurring with no setup fee, the promotional plans carry no refunds, and replying to the thread with an order number doubles the monthly bandwidth.

egress.terms: 2.5 TB a month counting both directions; no overage price and no post-allowance throttle stated
egress.free_allowance: 2.5 TB per month, inbound and outbound combined

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: VirtFusion control panel, Linux and Windows (bring your own licence), custom ISOs, a status page at status.ravnix.gg and a looking glass at atl-lg.ravnix.gg; no API is documented on the pages read
chaining: USD 14/year is USD 1.17/month for a 1 GB machine, which is the lowest annual rate, and the bidirectional bandwidth count is the reason to read the allowance before treating it as 2.5 TB of outbound; the EPYC-8 row at USD 10/month for 8 GB and 15 TB is the same host's answer for a heavier job

limits.value: 2.5 TB a month on the entry plan, and the thread states the count includes inbound as well as outbound, which halves the usable figure against every other record here that counts outbound only. 2.5 TB a month averages about 8 Mbit/s, so the counter binds far before the 500 Mbps port.

the vendor page confirms the price band and the site ('South Carolina', 'Starting $4/mo', 'Starting $3/mo', '99.9% Uptime SLA') but carries no plan table and no per-plan figures, and its location line does not match the thread's Atlanta
